name: The Wandering Isle
region_detail: Lake Ophar — reported at several widely separated positions.
location_category: Natural wonders; supernatural sites; ancient sites
site_type: island | Natural wonders; supernatural sites; ancient sites | Apparently mobile wooded island containing ancient ruins.
history: Namaris oral histories and generations of fishermen’s accounts describe a wooded island whose shoreline is recognizable despite its changing position. A small stone settlement once stood among its trees, but its builders and the circumstances of its abandonment are unknown.
current_state: The island is occasionally sighted outside the usual shipping lanes. Its wooded shore, unusual trees, and remnants of stone buildings distinguish it from ordinary islands. Navigation charts record conflicting sightings, and attempts to revisit its reported position have often failed. No explanation for its apparent movement has been established.
inhabitants: Woodland and shoreline wildlife; any other inhabitants, including the creature described in Namaris legend, remain undetermined.
danger_level: Low to moderate when approached in calm conditions; uncertain if the island moves or its ruins are disturbed.
points_of_interest:
Wooded shoreline; ancient trees; collapsed stone houses; a paved clearing; worn landing steps; an inland pool; unusual formations along the submerged shore.

Unresolved elements: Whether the island moves physically, appears in different places through magic, or is subject to another phenomenon; The origin and fate of the stone settlement; Whether the island is a living creature, as some stories claim; Whether visitors can predict its appearance or departure.
discovery: Lake Ophar — reported at several widely separated positions. Fishermen’s charts and Namaris stories preserve accounts of sightings. A current sighting may provide a more reliable lead than historical bearings.
discoverability: Conditional. Its position must be established through a current sighting or other reliable means of locating it.
